proposals.entity_key: Use of subjunctive after verbs of wish and desire
value: Je veux que tu achètes cet ordinateur.
Je veux acheter cet ordinateur. (same subject -> infinitive)

evidence.notes: Verbs of wish and desire take que plus the subjunctive when the two subjects differ; with the same subject an infinitive is used instead, as in the contrast given by the rule.

value: En France, on boit du vin.
On va au cinéma cet après-midi ?
Alors, on se promène au lieu de faire ses devoirs !

evidence.notes: On can mean one, people in general, informal nous, informal tu, or a passive equivalent; the examples match the five uses listed in the rule context.

proposals.entity_key: Using -ci and -là to distinguish between two elements
value: Tu préfères ce gâteau-ci ou ce gâteau-là ?

evidence.notes: The particles -ci and -là attach to the noun after the demonstrative adjective to mark proximity and distance; the last example uses the signal word ou.

value: On parle anglais ici. (English is spoken here.)
On demande un serveur. (A waiter is wanted.)
On vend des fruits au marché. (Fruit is sold at the market.)

evidence.notes: French often prefers an on plus third-person singular verb construction where English would use the passive voice.

value: venir -> je viens, tu viens, il vient, nous venons, vous venez, ils viennent
devenir -> je deviens, tu deviens, il devient, nous devenons, vous devenez, ils deviennent
prévenir -> je préviens, tu préviens, il prévient, nous prévenons, vous prévenez, ils préviennent
revenir -> je reviens, tu reviens, il revient, nous revenons, vous revenez, ils reviennent
survenir -> je surviens, tu surviens, il survient, nous survenons, vous survenez, ils surviennent

evidence.notes: Devenir, prévenir, revenir and survenir follow the same present-tense pattern as venir (stem vien- in the singular and third plural, ven- in nous and vous).

value: C'est moi qui lui ai vendu cette lampe.
C'est vous qui avez restauré cette chaise ?

evidence.notes: When qui is the subject of the dependent clause, the verb agrees with the pronoun it replaces after c'est; the first three examples come from the rule context.

proposals.entity_key: Verbs conjugated with être in passé composé

evidence.notes: The listed intransitive movement and state verbs take être in the passé composé and the past participle agrees with the subject.

proposals.entity_key: Verbs followed by preposition de before infinitive

evidence.notes: These verbs from the rule list are followed by de plus an infinitive; the elision d' is used before a vowel.

proposals.entity_key: Verbs followed by preposition à before infinitive

evidence.notes: These verbs from the rule list are followed by à plus an infinitive; they must not be confused with the verbs that take de.
These verbs from the rule list are followed directly by an infinitive with no preposition when both actions share the same subject.
